title: CPlane shift swap standup - 2026-05-18
content:
Attendees: Priya (owner), Ethan, Zara, Miguel, Lina, Amina (joined late)
Time: 09:15 - 09:45 PT
Context: Mid-rotation swap between day and night shifts. Quick sync focused on routing policy change rolled out yesterday, quota anomaly from 02:00-03:00 PT, and planned auth token rotation next week.

Top-line summary:
- Routing policy rollback partial: we rolled back one portion of the new tiered-routing change due to increased tail latency on small models. Top-95 latency rose from 120ms -> 220ms for short-sequence requests.
- Quota spike investigation: spike was correlated with a single customer's traffic pattern hitting many short-lived streams; throttles held but alarms climbed. No customer-visible errors.
- Auth rotation planning: we will perform a staged KMS-backed key rotation for the control plane auth tokens on Thu 2026-05-21 (canary in us-west1).

Detailed notes:
1) Routing (Ethan)
- What happened: New tiered-routing policy (PR #487) introduced a hop where requests for models < 2k tokens were evaluated differently; this caused unexpected batching behavior and increased serialization time.
- Evidence: trace ids: trace-20260518-01..08 show extra 12-28ms serialization per request on the routing path. Canary traffic was only ~5% so signal was noisy; full rollout at 30% amplified the tail.
- Action taken: rolled back the tiered decision node for small-model path at 03:10 PT. We left other changes (routing weights) intact.
- Next steps: Ethan to instrument per-path batching counts and add a synthetic load test for short-sequence distributions. ETA: instrumentation by 2026-05-20.
- Linked ticket: INF-2345 (root cause + mitigation).

2) Quotas & Billing Signals (Zara)
- Spike summary: 02:00-03:00 PT saw 4x normal allocation attempts for quota buckets Q-user-embed and Q-route-cache; token usage steady but attempt counts high due to many repeated ephemeral connections from one customer.
- Impact: autoscaler and quota service handled it; no service degradation, but we saw late-sample alerts in Ops and increased billing-metering churn.
- Mitigation: implemented a short-lived connection debounce (server side) for the specific customer pattern as a temporary measure. Longer-term: add per-connection attach metadata to detect ephemeral-churn patterns and apply soft limits.
- Action item: Zara to open PLT-1182 for debounce formalization and add test harness. ETA: design doc by 2026-05-22.

3) Auth (Miguel / Lina)
- Planned rotation: KMS key rotation for control-plane tokens. Goal: zero-downtime rotation with a small canary.
- Risks: cache invalidation across Dedicated pools and Private clusters may cause transient auth failures if clients keep long-lived token caches.
- Mitigations: 1) staged rollout: canary (us-west1) -> regional rollouts -> global; 2) extend dual-signature window to 48h during rollout; 3) notify SRE and CS for high-risk enterprise customers.
- Outstanding: need a quick script to verify token acceptance across old+new keys for each deployment type. Lina to provide script. ETA: 2026-05-20.
- Communication: Priya to draft email to Enterprise accounts impacted by Private deployments by EOD 2026-05-18.

4) Observability / Alerts (Amina joined)
- Alert fatigue: Ops saw repeated RateLimitExceeded alerts during the quota spike; suggestion to add a suppression window for repeated alerts from the same resource in 10m windows.
- Tracing: need better end-to-end trace sampling for short requests — current sampling biases toward long flows. We want consistent tail visibility for <200ms flows.
- Action: add an experimental low-latency sampling config in staging. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2026-05-21.

5) Incident backlog and follow-ups
- INF-2345: routing serialization root cause (assigned Ethan).
- PLT-1182: quota debounce and test harness (assigned Zara).
- SEC-rot-9: auth rotation checklist (assigned Miguel + Lina).
- OBS-409: trace sampling for short flows (assigned Ethan).

Quick wins / small TODOs
- Add a dashboard widget for per-path batching size distribution (Priya volunteered to sketch).
- Update the runbook 'routing-rollout' to include a quick rollback checklist (2 engineers, 5 minutes). Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-05-19.
- Create a short Slack postmortem for the quota spike to share with CS and billing teams. Owner: Zara. ETA: 2026-05-18.

Parking lot / questions to escalate
- Should we change the default client token TTL to 3h for Dedicated tiers given observed long-lived connections? Pros/cons discussion deferred to Thursday planning.
- Need clarity on the planned cadence of routing experiments: monthly vs weekly? Ops prefers monthly to reduce churn. Put on agenda for platform retro.

Risks / blockers
- Auth rotation script dependency on internal KMS SDK patch (blocking until 2026-05-20).
- Load test harness for short flows currently does not mimic library-level batching; need improvement to replicate real behavior.

Meeting close & owners recap:
- Ethan: instrumentation for per-path batching, trace-sampling experiment, INF-2345 fix branch.
- Zara: design doc for debounce (PLT-1182), Slack postmortem for spike.
- Miguel + Lina: auth rotation checklist + verification script, SEC-rot-9 prep.
- Priya: routing-rollout runbook update, enterprise notifications, dashboard sketch.

Next sync: 2026-05-19 09:15 PT (hand-off to night shift). Expect short async updates on tickets; escalate to #platform-controlplane if new customer impact observed.

Notes to self (informal):
- Capture a small clip of traces showing serialization step — helpful for oncall handoff.
- Remind infra to increase sampling retention for 48h for the canary window.

End of notes.
